newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian minister linked to scandal resigns - agency.
newsitem.headline: Indian minister linked to scandal resigns - agency.

text.p: Indian junior Rural Areas and Employment Minister Chandradeo Prasad Varma, accused in a $280-million corruption scandal, resigned on Friday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The news agency said the minister stepped down on the request of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, whose Janata Dal party has been rocked by the animal fodder scandal.
Varma is one of several dozen accused in the scandal in the eastern state of Bihar.
On Tuesday, the governor of the eastern state of Bihar authorised federal police to prosecute Varma and the state chief minister, Laloo Prasad Yadav, in the corruption case.
Both Yadav and Varma have said they are innocent in the scandal, which dates back to the 1980s and involves the alleged siphoning off of animal welfare funds.

Leftwing parties in Gujral's centre-left United Front alliance have been pressing for Yadav and Varma to step down. Yadav has refused to quit as chief minister and is running in party elections to retain his post as Janata Dal president.
